Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae and some bacteria turn light energy into chemical energy. In the chloroplasts, chlorophyll absorbs mostly blue and red light; that energy splits water molecules, releasing oxygen, and drives the production of ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle these carriers then fix carbon dioxide from the air into three-carbon sugars, which the plant builds into glucose, starch and cellulose. Almost every food chain on Earth starts here, and the oxygen in the atmosphere is its by-product.
